title: Using fluorescent indicators for in vivo quantification of spontaneous or evoked motor neuron presynaptic activity in transgenic zebrafish
protocol: Prepare an injection solution of 3–13 pg/nL plasmid DNA (mnx1:SypHy-p2a-mRFP) in deoxyribonuclease and ribonuclease-free water.
Backfill 10 μl of plasmid solution into embryo injection needle.
Insert the injection needle into a glass pipette holder clamped onto a micromanipulator.
Examine the injected larvae under a fluorescent stereo microscope to visualize transgene expression for identifying optimal plasmid concentration.
Break the tip of the injection needle to create a tip opening diameter of around 20–25 μm, preferably with a beveled tip.
Calibrate droplet diameter to 120 μm for a 1 nL volume by suspending in mineral oil on micron slide.
Collect zebrafish embryos within 20 min of spawning.
Microinject into single cell of zebrafish zygotes at the one-cell stage.
Stabilize zebrafish zygotes in a 1.5% agarose plate within troughs formed by a plastic mold.
Incubate embryos in petri dishes filled with E3 embryo media at 28.5°C, with 50–100 embryos per dish.
Remove unfertilized or abnormal embryos at 3–4 h post-fertilization.
Continue to remove abnormal or dead embryos at least every other day starting from 1 dpf.
Prepare an injection solution of 7 pg/nL pDestTol2CG2-5kbneuroD:G-GECO plasmid DNA and 100 pg/nL Tol2 transposase mRNA in deoxyribonuclease and ribonuclease-free water.
Backfill plasmid solution into embryo injection needle.
Insert the injection needle into a glass pipette holder clamped onto a micromanipulator.
Calibrate droplet diameter to 120 μm for a 1 nL volume suspended in mineral oil over micron slide.
Collect zebrafish embryos within 20 min of spawning.
Microinject into zebrafish zygotes at the one cell stage.
Screen injected embryos (F0) at 2–4 dpf for G-GECO expression in neurons of interest.
Raise G-GECO expressing F0 embryos to reproductive maturity.
Outcross F0 transgenic zebrafish with wild type and screen the progeny embryos (F1) for transgene expression in neurons of interest.
Raise G-GECO expressing F1 embryos to reproductive maturity.
Outcross heterozygous F1 zebrafish to create heterozygous F2 zebrafish.
Identify lines with a single transgenic insertion event by assessing larvae for transgene expression on a fluorescent stereo microscope.
Raise zygotes injected with plasmid DNA encoding mnx1:SypHy-p2a-mRFP to 4 dpf.
Sort larvae for expression of the mRFP reporter in the cell body of spinal motor neurons of the ventral spinal cord on a fluorescent stereo microscope.
Group sorted larvae based on whether neurons expressing fluorescent reporters are on the left or right side of the larvae by placing each group in a separate dish containing E3 embryo media.
Melt low melt agarose in water near boiling temperature and incubate in 42°C water bath to equilibrate.
Secure new coverslip to the top of the punched petri dish lid using vacuum grease.
Anesthetize larvae in fresh E3 embryo media with 0.02% tricaine.
Wash larvae briefly in fresh embryo media to remove the tricaine.
Mount larvae in 1.8% low-melt agarose.
Dispense larvae suspended in minimal volume of E3 into agarose using a glass pipette.
Pipette the larvae, now suspended in agarose solution, onto coverslip mounted on 35 mm punched petri dish lid.
Gently press the side of the larva with the expressing neuron onto the coverslip while the agarose is fluid.
Minimize the gap between the surface of the larva and coverslip using a fine embryo manipulator.
Embed larvae in agarose within 1 min following removal of tricaine.
Submerge solidified low-melt agarose in embryo media by placing the lid on the 35 mm petri dish bottom filled with embryo media.
Wrap edge with parafilm to avoid spillage.
Identify a motor neuron axon terminal of interest.
Under brightfield or phase contrast illumination on a confocal microscope, identify the ventral spinal cord with a 10× objective.
Add water for immersion to the coverslip.

With a 63× (NA1.2) water immersion objective, identify the cell body of the targeted motor neuron using the cytosolic mRFP and trace its axon through the trunk to a terminal on the surface of the trunk near the horizontal myoseptum.
Adjust the focal planes for a z-stack of the region.
Capture mRFP and SypHy signals using 561 nm and 488 nm excitation lasers.
Optimize z-resolution in a stack every 10 seconds for 5 minutes.
Acquire 30 image stacks.
Ensure images are taken with optimal parameters for best resolution on your confocal system.
Use sequential imaging without averaging for typical point-scanning confocal microscopes to allow sufficient temporal resolution.
Maintain consistent microscope settings (laser power, detector sensitivity and offset) between larvae imaged for the experiment.
Repeat the procedure for at least 10 animals per group.
Incubate neurons in 100 mM N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) to increase spontaneous release frequency.
Anesthetize larvae in fresh E3 embryo media with 0.02% tricaine (0.4% tricaine diluted 1/20 in E3).
Mount the anesthetized larvae near the surface of a droplet of 1.8% low-melt agarose lying on one side.
Position 4 dpf G-GECO expressing larva for imaging to measure evoked motor neuron synaptic calcium influx at the neuromuscular junction.
Use fine forceps (#5 or #55) to cut two shallow lines parallel to each side of the tail.
Cut around the tail to free it from agarose.
Lift the agarose free of the tail using fine forceps (#5 or #55).
Submerge the larva in embryo media with 0.02% tricaine to immobilize the larva for heart injection.
Load needle with α-bungarotoxin for heart injection.
Backfill heart injection needle with 3 μL α-bungarotoxin colored with phenol red to visually confirm injection.
Insert the heart injection needle into a pipette holder clamped to a micromanipulator next to a stereo microscope.
Connect the pipette holder to a pressure injector with Pinjection = 100 hPa, tinjection = 0.5 s, and Pcompensation = 5 hPa.
Position the pipette holder at a 30° angle from horizontal towards the DV axis of an immobilized larva.
Use the heart injection needle to penetrate through the low-melt agarose into the cardiac cavity under the stereo microscope.
Inject one pulse into the cardiac cavity using the recommended pressure injector settings.
Rinse the paralyzed larva with three washes of embryo media to remove tricaine.
Prepare a new larva if the heartbeat is impacted or significantly slowed down during rinsing.
Place the larvae under the objective of a confocal microscope with stimulation capability.
Backfill the fluid-jet needle with embryo media for fluid-jet stimulation preparation.
Score the tip of the fluid-jet needle perpendicularly against a ceramic tile to create an opening with an inner diameter between 35 and 50 μm.
Ensure that the break is even across the tip for well-directed flow.
Position the fluid jet near the tail under phase contrast with a 10× objective of the confocal.
Adjust the pressure output and visually confirm that the tail and tail fin are deflected without shifting the body of the larva.
Set the back pressure such that the fluid jet pipette is not deflecting the tail at rest.
Visually confirm by moving the pipette away from and back toward the tail; the tail should not move.
Locate somite 4, which may be identified by counting the chevron-shaped body segments that span the dorsal-ventral axis of the trunk.
Draw an arbitrary straight line across the width of the imaged motor neuron axon to specify the region of interest.
Use the signal intensity measured across the line to determine the half-max intensity.
Set the half-max intensity as the lower threshold limit.
Define the pixels included in the measurement based on the lower threshold limit.
Visualize evoked synaptic calcium activity within the motor neuron axon following tail stimulation delivery, indicated with a heatmap overlay.
Take baseline intensity from the average of the 2 seconds prior to stimulation delivery.
Switch to a 60× (NA 1.0) dipping objective to identify an imaging plane of interest.
Trace the motor neuron axon from the spinal cord until reaching a superficially located bulbous axon terminal dorsal to the horizontal myoseptum but slightly ventral to the spinal cord is identified.
Test the fluid-jet pressure to ensure the imaging plane remains in focus during stimulation.
Capture the G-GECO signal using a 488 nm excitation laser every 50 ms for 10 seconds, yielding 200 images.
Deliver a 50 ms pulse of fluid at 5 seconds after starting image acquisition.
Collect at least 12 measurements for each group.
Separate multiple stimulation attempts by a 2 minute rest period.
Import image sequence for analysis into FIJI using the Bio-formats plugin.
Select Area and Mean gray value as measurement values in the “Set Measurement” window under “Analyze”.
Generate sum-projected z-stacks of the axon terminal through the time series.
Outline the axon terminal to be analyzed using the freehand tool.
Record the mean fluorescence intensity for the SypHy channel separately.
Record the mean fluorescence intensity for the mRFP channel separately.
Calculate the average mean fluorescence intensity of SypHy normalized to the mean fluorescence intensity of mRFP across entire time series.
Compare data sets using ANOVA if parametric or Wilcoxon rank sums if nonparametric.
Install the Image Stabilizer plugin in FIJI.
Select “Set Measurement” window under “Analyze” menu.
Check boxes for “Area”, “Mean gray value”, and “Add to overlay”.
Import acquired images with FIJI.
Register X-Y movement artifacts using the Image Stabilizer plugin.
Go to frame 60, or 3 seconds after imaging began.
Draw a line region of interest (ROI) across an arbitrary axis of the visible motor neuron.
Include some background on each end of the line.
Open the “Plot Profile” window under “Analyze” menu.
Plot the intensity value across the line.
Calculate the average between the maximum and minimum intensity values.
Use the calculated half-max value as the minimum threshold to segment the image into regions.
Use the threshold tool to segment the image from the half-max to the maximum value.
Create an ROI around the area above the threshold using “Create selection” under “Edit”, in the “Selection” sub header.
Open the “Roi manager” window and add the newly created ROI.
In the “Roi manager”, use “Multi measure” to record the values for the mean intensity for each time point on a spreadsheet, and record the area measured for this time series.
Save the ROI containing the axon of interest in the .roi file format using the ROI Manager window.
Plot the change in intensity over baseline by calculating ((F-F0)/ F0), where F is the fluorescence measurement of each frame and F0 is the average of the 2 seconds before stimulation (frame 60–99).
Collect the maximum value after stimulation onset for each time series from the calculated changes in intensity.
Perform the appropriate statistical analysis on the peak change in intensity using ANOVA if the data sets meet normal distribution criteria.
